To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the giant glial cells in the leech nervous system have a K+ conductances that is modulated by Na+ but is independent of Ca2+.
Na+ removal from the saline causes an increase in the membrane conductance of the leech giant reticular glial cell, which can be attributed to an increase in a K+ conductane.
Na+ modulate a K+ conductances of the giant glia cells in leeches, which is independent of intra and extra cellular Ca2+ concentration.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the regulation of the membrane conductance of the leech glial cells and its relation with the intracellular Na+ concentration.
the study of ion channels and transporters in the glial cells of the leech.
the study of the mechanisms of the Na+-dependent regulation of K+ conductance in the glial cells of the leech.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
a Na+-dependent K+ conductance in the glial cell membrane of the leech giant axon is independent of Ca2+.
the glial cell is a K+ buffer, which is modulated by the Na+ concentration in the extracellular fluid.
a sodium-sensitive potassium conductance is present in the giant glial cells of the leech.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
Na+ removal from the extracellular fluid of the giant glia increases the membrane conductance by activating a Na+ independent K+ conductance, which does not depend on Ca2+.
Na+-sensitive K+ channels exist in glial cells and that these channels are Ca2+-independent.
the giant glial cells of the leech are not as sensitive to Na+ as other cell types.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Na+-sensitive, Ca2+-independent K+ conductance in glial cells can be studied in the leech, and the leech can be used as a model system for the study of glial K+ conductances.
the glial cells of the leech are not as sensitive to changes in the extracellular Ca2+ concentration as are the glial cells from the rat.
glial cells can be modulated by extracellular ions and this can be a way to regulate their activity in the nervous system.
